payload.summary: Directive 2003/87/EC (EU ETS) grounds the ETS 1 scope determination (Art. 2, Art. 3(e), Annex I), the monitoring/reporting of installation emissions (Art. 14, Annex IV calculation method), the surrender obligation (Art. 12(3)) and verification (Art. 15). These support surfacing site-identity, activity-category, energy-consumption, emission-factor and reported-emissions fields needed to build the assurance memo. Note the directive governs direct installation emissions and annual calendar-year reporting; the registry's Scope 2 indirect-emissions framing, quarterly cadence, 5% discrepancy rule, and the size/BU organizational filters are not defined in the directive text and are recorded as missing context.

selected_pages.reason: Article 2 (scope) and Article 3(e) (definition of installation as a stationary technical unit carrying Annex I activities) ground ETS 1 scope determination.
Article 12(3) sets the surrender obligation of allowances equal to verified total emissions, cited by the registry.
Article 14 (monitoring and reporting of emissions) and Article 15 (verification) ground the monitoring-assurance basis and the reported-emissions requirement.
Annex I lists the categories of activities and capacity thresholds that determine whether a manufacturing installation falls within ETS 1 scope.
Annex IV defines the emissions calculation method (activity data × emission factor × oxidation factor) and the reporting data elements, grounding the energy-derived computation method.

findings.statement: The Directive applies to emissions from the activities listed in Annex I and to the greenhouse gases listed in Annex II, defining the boundary of ETS 1 coverage.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Article 2 Scope 1. This Directive shall apply to emissions from the activities listed in Annex I and greenhouse gases listed in Annex II.

findings.statement: An 'installation' is a stationary technical unit where one or more Annex I activities are carried out, plus directly associated technically connected activities that could affect emissions.
findings.evidence_excerpt: 'installation' means a stationary technical unit where one or more activities listed in Annex I are carried out and any other directly associated activities which have a technical connection with the activities carried out on that site and which could have an effect on emissions.

findings.statement: Annex I lists categories of activities (energy, ferrous metals, mineral industry, pulp/paper, etc.) with capacity thresholds; only installations exceeding these thresholds are covered, and research/development/testing installations are excluded.
findings.evidence_excerpt: CATEGORIES OF ACTIVITIES ... Combustion installations with a rated thermal input exceeding 20 MW ... Installations for the production of pig iron or steel ... with a capacity exceeding 2,5 tonnes per hour.

findings.statement: Member States shall ensure emissions are monitored per the Commission guidelines and that each operator reports the emissions from that installation during each calendar year to the competent authority.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Article 14 ... 2. Member States shall ensure that emissions are monitored in accordance with the guidelines. 3. Member States shall ensure that each operator of an installation reports the emissions from that installation during each calendar year.

findings.statement: Emissions may be monitored by calculation using Activity data × Emission factor × Oxidation factor, with activity data (fuel used, production rate) and accepted emission factors; a separate calculation is made for each activity, installation and fuel.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Calculations of emissions shall be performed using the formula: Activity data × Emission factor × Oxidation factor. Activity data (fuel used, production rate etc.) shall be monitored on the basis of supply data or measurement.

findings.statement: By 30 April each year the operator of each installation must surrender allowances equal to the total verified emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Article 12 ... 3. Member States shall ensure that, by 30 April each year at the latest, the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year as verified in accordance with Article 15.

findings.statement: Reports submitted under Article 14(3) must be verified against Annex V criteria; a report is satisfactory only if total emissions are not materially misstated.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Article 15 Verification Member States shall ensure that the reports submitted by operators pursuant to Article 14(3) are verified in accordance with the criteria set out in Annex V.

No catalog column indicates whether a unit is a stationary technical installation per the ETS Art. 3(e) test. This scope-determination attribute is absent from the runtime catalog. Expected non-failing unmapped result.
No oxidation-factor column or requestable measure exists in the catalog. The Annex IV oxidation factor is not represented and cannot be invented. Expected non-failing unmapped result.

The catalog has no operator-identity column. sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This memo is an ETS 1 monitoring-assurance review of the the company large-manufacturing site portfolio for FY2025 Q4 through FY2026 Q2. For each site and quarter it reproduces one quarterly Scope 2 CO₂e claim by two independent methods and reconciles them into a single per-site-per-quarter conclusion, with directive-article grounding. The regulatory frame is Directive 2003/8*/EC (EU ETS): Annex IV grounds the energy-derived calculation approach, Art. 14(*) grounds the monitoring-and-reporting obligation, and Art. 15 / Annex V frame verification. This deliverable is for compliance-team review and is not a formal regulatory filing. Note that several sites lie outside the EU/EEA (Canada, United States, China, Serbia); for those the directive framing is applied only as portfolio methodology and ETS 1 installation status is not established.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.body: Method A (energy-derived) is the Annex IV 'activity data × emission factor' product, surfaced as scope2_market_proxy_t (amount_consumed_mwh × co2_factor, Scope 2 rows) per R2F-001. Method B (reported Scope 2) is the directly-reported figure scope2_location_t (co2e_t, Scope 2 rows) per R2F-002, aligned with the Art. 14(*) reporting obligation. The dual-method cross-check (R2F-003) compares the absolute delta between the two figures as a material-misstatement test, flagging any case where |delta| exceeds *% of the higher value. This *% threshold is an analytical/QA criterion not defined in the directive — Annex V refers only qualitatively to emissions 'not being materially misstated' — so agreement here is a cross-check, not a formal Article 1* verification. The embedded co2_factor and oxidation factor are not independently exposed, so a factor-by-factor Annex IV decomposition could not be performed.
